sub1: Weekday Lates with the 08:30–17:00 turns moved into the evening — the same people, the same hours, rearranged to sit under the 17:00 peak
h3: What moved, and what it cost
sub3: Two lines changed turn; nothing else in the table did
coverNote: gaps of 8, 6, 5, 5 around the wheel — inherited from Weekday Lates, not re-spread
methodHeading: Why the evening was thin, and what was changed
sub7: Reproducible: the same starting grid, seed and objective give the same rotation on any machine
method:
1 · The cause was a cliff, not a shortage. Nine duties in Weekday Lates ran 08:30–17:00 and every one of them finished at the same moment. Weekday cover therefore fell from eight, nine or ten people at 16:00 to six from 17:00 — at exactly the hour the December traffic curve peaks, at about 140 cars an hour against 110 at 16:00. Cover was going down as demand went up.

2 · Two lines changed turn, and nothing else did. Line 9's week moved from 08:30–17:00 to 12:30–21:00, and line 16's Monday to Wednesday to 14:00–22:30. Both replacements are 8h30, the same length as the turn they replace, so the contracted week is still paid to the minute without anything else moving. Both lines stay one-turn weeks — nobody is asked to hold two different start times in one week.

3 · Then the shape was searched, not the staffing. The same two moves as the other repaired proposal — swap a duty within one day column, or swap two whole lines — so the new coverage curve is invariant by construction and is asserted to be identical before and after. That took the longest run from 9 to 6, the factors present from 5 to 1, and FF8b from 5 to none.
openQuestions: This is a trade, and it cannot not be. At a fixed 35-hour week every hour added to the evening comes from somewhere else, so the honest figures are both directions: 17:00–21:00 goes from 6, 6, 7, 9, 8 across Monday to Friday to 8, 8, 9, 10, 9, and 08:00–11:00 falls from 7, 9, 8, 7, 8 to 5, 7, 6, 6, 7. The morning still meets the four-to-open rule everywhere, and the December curve does run lighter before 09:00 than at 17:00 — but Monday morning at five is the thinnest point in this design and is the thing to look at before agreeing it. If that is too thin, moving line 16 alone rather than both lines lifts the evening to 7, 7, 8, 9, 8 and leaves the morning at 6, 8, 7, 7, 8; it is the row below this proposal in the table opposite. Sunday's finish is unchanged and still inherits today's window.
